title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company; the general population to whom this Policy applies alongside all Group employees.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All employees of the Group; the base insider trading and hedging rules in sections 3 and 6.3(a)-(c) apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors, Senior Executives and Nominated Employees, collectively. Subject to blackout periods, prior approval for dealing, confirmation of trade, no short-term dealing, and the margin lending ban under sections 5 and 6.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Officers and other direct reports of the Chief Executive Officer; must obtain approval from the Chief Executive Officer before dealing.

tiers.name: Nominated Employees
tiers.description: Other persons who regularly possess Inside Information and have been advised by the Company Secretary that they are subject to special restrictions; approval regime is the same as for Senior Executives (Chief Executive Officer).

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair; must obtain approval from the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee rather than the Chair of the Board.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may influence or be influenced by the employee or director (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, dependants), and a company or other entity the employee or director can control.

participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company. However, where securities in the Company granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy;
acquisition of Company securities through a dividend reinvestment plan;
acquisition of Company securities through a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders; acquisition of Company securities through a rights issue;
the disposal of Company securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back;

dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of Company securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the employee, director or their Connected Person is a beneficiary);

trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the employee, director or their Connected Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the employee, director or their Connected Person to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period, other than in exceptional circumstances;
a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

exemption_authority: The Chief Executive Officer (for Senior Executives, Nominated Employees and their Connected Persons), the Chair of the Board (for directors and their Connected Persons), or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee (for the Chair and his/her Connected Persons) may approve dealing during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order, provided the applicant holds no Inside Information; approval runs for 2 business days. Separately, a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights (e.g. under a margin lending arrangement) is excluded from the Policy's blackout and approval requirements without needing any exemption.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging of vested unrestricted shares expressly permitted
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and their Connected Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities provided that the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications required under section 5 are made on that basis.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the key collar-relevant clause: the policy expressly contemplates hedging vested, unrestricted shares by Restricted Persons subject only to ordinary section 5 dealing approvals, which is unusually favourable compared to policies that ban hedging outright.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending scope narrower than secured financing
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and their Connected Persons must not deal in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The express ban only reaches arrangements badged as margin lending; a bank collar loan structured as a general secured facility may sit outside the literal wording, though the section 10 substance-over-form approach creates real risk the Company would still treat it as caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the collar's secured loan is not literally a 'margin lending arrangement', this clause signals the Company would likely still treat an economically equivalent secured facility as caught by the section 6.2 ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly excluded from the blackout-period and pre-approval requirements, giving the bank a clean enforcement path even during a closed period, provided the sale is genuinely lender-driven rather than voluntary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The short-term dealing ban expressly extends to forward-contract-style arrangements, so a short-tenor collar entered and unwound by a Restricted Person within three months would independently breach this rule regardless of the hedging permission.

bespoke_clauses.topic: transfer into margin account is a dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a bank requires the collared shares to be moved into a collateral or margin-style account to secure the loan, that transfer is itself treated as a prohibited dealing for Restricted Persons, so custody arrangements need careful structuring.

summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable under this policy, which is unusually explicit on the point: section 6.3(d) expressly permits Restricted Persons to hedge vested, unrestricted Company securities provided the hedge is treated as a dealing and cleared under section 5 (approval from the CEO, Chair of the Board, or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee as applicable, valid for 2 business days, outside blackout periods or via the exceptional-circumstances process). The obstacle is the loan leg: section 6.2 bans Restricted Persons from dealing in Company securities 'in connection with a margin lending arrangement', including transferring shares into a margin account or selling to satisfy a margin call, and the Company's stated substance-over-form approach (section 10) means a bank facility economically equivalent to margin lending would likely be caught even if not literally badged as one. If the loan is nonetheless found to be a 'margin lending arrangement', a lender's enforcement sale is expressly excluded from the blackout and approval rules, giving the bank a clear enforcement path on default. Tenor must exceed three months given the express extension of the short-term dealing ban to forward contracts, and unvested or holding-locked shares can never be hedged or used as collateral.
